facts.claim: Brown et al. (2020) showed GPT-3, a 175-billion-parameter model, doing new tasks from a few worked examples placed in the prompt, with no change to its weights.

Zhao et al. (2021) found that the examples in a prompt, and their order, can swing a model’s accuracy from near chance to near the best results, because it leans towards answers it saw near the end or saw often.
Liu et al. (2023) found that models use information best near the start or the end of a long input, and noticeably worse in the middle.
Anthropic’s prompting guide (checked October 2026) says to treat the model as a brilliant but new employee who lacks your context: the more precisely you explain what you want, the better the result.
Anthropic’s prompting guide (checked October 2026) calls examples one of the most reliable ways to steer a reply’s format, tone and structure, and suggests three to five of them.
Anthropic’s prompting guide (checked October 2026) says to put long documents near the top and the question at the end, which improved reply quality by up to 30% in its tests.

OpenAI’s prompt engineering guide (checked October 2026) advises marking a prompt’s sections with Markdown or XML tags, giving examples of inputs with the outputs you want, pinning production apps to a model snapshot, and building evals that measure prompt behaviour.
Nemotron 3 Ultra is NVIDIA’s mixture-of-experts model with 550 billion parameters, 55 billion of them active for each token.
gpt-oss-20b is OpenAI’s smaller open-weight model, with about 21 billion parameters, 3.6 billion of them active for each token.
